summary: Verified all 3 UX rewires (Hero Reserve-direct-modal, Hero See-menu -> /suppers chooser, Admin Reservations toggle) end-to-end on backend + frontend. Added 3 new pytest cases for /api/settings + /api/admin/settings + 403-when-closed gate on POST /events/{id}/register. Full backend regression: 44/44 PASS (previous 41 + 3 new). Frontend Playwright verified: (a) hero-see-menu-button navigates to /suppers and renders both 'Series concluded' Naani Ghar and 'Work in progress' Barsaat cards with correct links/buttons, (b) supper-barsaat-prebook opens EventRegistrationModal with a visible 'A note before you reserve' banner carrying data-testid='reg-disclaimer', (c) hero-reserve-seat-button opens EventRegistrationModal directly pre-filled with 'Barsaat — Monsoon Edition' / 2026-08-15 / 19:30-22:00, (d) Admin Overview toggle (registrations-toggle) flips registrations_open in /api/settings instantly with success toast, (e) when closed: hero CTA label becomes 'Reservations closed · Join list', click does NOT open modal, and direct POST /events/{id}/register returns 403 with friendly message 'Reservations are currently closed. Please check back soon.', (f) toggling back ON restores normal flow. Final registrations_open restored to true.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1065 lines — approaching the soft 700-line cap. Consider splitting into modules (routes_auth.py, routes_events.py, routes_registrations.py, routes_cms.py, routes_settings.py) before adding more endpoints. The settings + CMS sections are natural extraction candidates.

PUT /api/admin/settings accepts a raw dict and silently drops unknown keys (filter `if k in DEFAULT_SETTINGS`). This is safe but returns 200 even if the client sent only invalid keys (no-op write). Consider returning 400 when no recognized key is present, or at least logging it, to help admins detect typos.

Suppers.jsx: when registrations_open=false, the pre-book button still appears clickable and only shows a toast on click — visually it would be clearer to dim/disable it (or swap label to 'Join the list') the same way Hero already does. Minor UX polish only.

The 403 'closed' check in register_event runs BEFORE the event-not-found check. This means an attacker probing for valid event IDs while registrations are closed cannot distinguish existing vs missing events (good for privacy). Keep this ordering.

_get_settings() merges DEFAULT_SETTINGS into stored data on every read — this is defensive and good: newly-added default keys auto-appear without migration. Same pattern as _deep_merge in CMS. Consistent.
